ety.text: From net + work; the nonliteral sense and its subsenses are extended from the literal sense; they are now the dominant senses. Cognate with German Netzwerk.

senses.d: Any interconnected group or system.
ex: A network of roads crisscrossed the country.
The many species that live in the forest canopy constitute a network of life via their complex interactions.

senses.d: A set of people with sociocultural connections to one another; especially, such a set consisting of occupational or business connections.
ex: To get a job in today's economy, it is important to have a strong network.
For people with mental health challenges, having a support network of family and friends can improve the chances of maintaining successful mental health care.

senses.d: A group of affiliated television stations that broadcast common programs from a parent company.
A computer network: multiple computers and other devices connected together to share information.
ex: The copy machine is connected to the network so it can now serve as a printer.

senses.d: A fabric or structure of fibrous elements attached to each other at regular intervals; the act or process of making such an object.
ex: He wore a mantle of network.

senses.d: To interact socially for the purpose of getting connections or personal advancement.
ex: Many people find it worthwhile to network for jobs and information.
The yuppies networking and / The panic, the vomit

senses.d: To connect two or more computers or other computerized devices.
ex: If we network his machine to the server, he will be able to see all the files.

senses.d: To interconnect a group or system.
To broadcast across an entire network of stations and affiliates at the same time.

senses.d: A mesh of string, cord or rope.
ex: a hairnet; a mosquito net; a tennis net

senses.d: A device made from such mesh, used for catching fish, butterflies, etc.
A device made from such mesh, generally used for trapping something.
Anything that has the appearance of such a device.
ex: Petri net

senses.d: A trap.
ex: caught in the prosecuting attorney's net
A man that flattereth his neighbor spreadeth a net for his feet.

senses.d: Any set of polygons joined edge to edge that, when folded along the edges between adjoining polygons so that the outer edges touch, form a given polyhedron.
A system that interconnects a number of users, locations etc. allowing transport or communication between them.
A conductor that interconnects two or more component terminals.
A framework backed by a mesh, serving as the goal in hockey, soccer, lacrosse, etc.
ex: The striker headed the ball into the net to make it 1-0.
Wigan had N'Zogbia sent off late on but Squillaci headed into his own net to give the home side a deserved point.

senses.d: A mesh stretched to divide the court in tennis, badminton, volleyball, etc.
To catch by means of a net.
To catch in a trap, or by stratagem.
ex: And now I am here, netted and in the toils.

senses.d: To enclose or cover with a net.
ex: Net the cherry trees to keep birds out.

senses.d: To score (a goal).
ex: Evans netted the winner in the 80th minute.
Romeu then scored a penalty, Torres netted a header and Moses added the sixth from substitute Oscar's cross.

senses.d: To hit the ball into the net.
To form a netting or network; to knit.
ex: I was shown into a pretty but rather close drawing-room, and there sat Agnes, netting a purse.

senses.d: Free from extraneous substances; pure; unadulterated; neat.
ex: net wine

senses.d: Remaining after expenses or deductions.
ex: Near-synonym: take-home
net profit; net weight

senses.d: Final; end.
ex: net result; net conclusion

senses.d: Good, desirable; clean, decent, clear.
ex: Her brest all naked, as net iuory, / Without adorne of gold or siluer bright […]

senses.d: After expenses or deductions.
ex: You'll have $5000 net.

senses.d: The amount remaining after expenses or other kinds of deductions are subtracted.
ex: Our net on that transaction was only fourteen dollars.
The net on that container was only fourteen tons.

senses.d: To receive as profit.
ex: The company nets $30 on every sale.

senses.d: To yield as profit for.
ex: The scam netted the criminals $30,000.

senses.d: To fully hedge a position.
ex: Every party is netting their position with a counter-party.

senses.d: To clean, wash, rinse.
